questions.prompt: Put the first-contact steps in the safest order.
questions.explain: Install, verify, enter a throwaway folder, then start the agent: each step makes the next one safer.
items: cd into an empty scratch folder

why.Confirm with claude --version: Install first, then confirm; a version cannot be checked until something is installed.
why.cd into an empty scratch folder: Move into the scratch folder after the install is confirmed and before you start the agent.
why.Start claude in plan mode: Start the agent last, after you are standing in a throwaway folder.
why.Run the installer: The installer comes first; everything else depends on it.

questions.prompt: After installing, your shell says `claude: command not found`. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: The launcher is in ~/.local/bin, so add that folder to PATH.

options.text: ~/.local/bin, where the launcher lives, is not on your PATH
Your Team plan login expired, so the shell blocks the program
options.misconception: Login happens after the program starts. A 'command not found' means the shell cannot find the program at all.

options.text: The installer needs sudo, so it quietly installed nothing
options.misconception: The launcher is installed under your own home folder and does not need root. The shell just cannot see that folder.

options.text: The ~/.claude folder is missing, so the command cannot be found
options.misconception: ~/.claude holds settings and credentials. The launcher is in ~/.local/bin, which the shell must be able to find.

questions.prompt: Match each permission mode to what it does.
questions.explain: Modes trade convenience for control. Plan mode is the safest for first contact.

pairs.right: Asks the first time each tool is used
Auto-accepts file edits and common file commands in the working directory
pairs.misconception: acceptEdits accepts edits without prompting. plan is the read-only mode.

pairs.right: Reads and runs read-only commands, leaves source untouched
Skips prompts; use only in containers or VMs
pairs.misconception: bypassPermissions removes the safety prompts, which is why it belongs in disposable environments.

questions.prompt: You have a Team subscription login AND `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` exported. What is the problem?
questions.explain: Run /status to see which credential is active.

options.text: The key wins once approved, so usage bills to your API account rather than your plan
None: the subscription always takes priority, so the key is simply ignored
options.misconception: The docs say the key wins once approved. Check /status and unset the variable if you did not mean to use it.

options.text: Claude Code refuses to start until you unset one of the two credentials
options.misconception: It starts fine, which is why the mix-up is easy to miss.

options.text: It asks you to pick a credential each session and bills whichever you choose
options.misconception: It asks once to approve the key. After that the key is used, so check /status.

questions.explain: doctor reports; you decide what to fix.

options.text: Prints read-only diagnostics about your installation
Repairs a broken install and reinstalls the launcher
options.misconception: doctor reports and leaves repairs to you. Read what it prints and fix the cause yourself.

options.text: Sends your session history to Anthropic for review
options.misconception: The shell command prints diagnostics without starting a session, so there is no session history to review.

options.text: Scans your project files for secrets before each session
options.misconception: doctor reports on the installation only. It does not scan project files for secrets.

questions.prompt: Match each question to the command that answers it.
questions.explain: Each command shows one slice of the setup. Pick by the question you have.

pairs.misconception: /mcp lists MCP servers and their connection status.

pairs.left: What is filling my context window?
pairs.misconception: /context breaks context use down by category.

pairs.left: Which installed skills never get used?
pairs.misconception: /skill-doctor reports per-skill cost and usage and flags skills that were never invoked.

pairs.left: claude will not even start. What do I run in the shell?
